claim: Any nonadaptive family of radius-three Hamming balls that identifies every vertex of the eight-cube must contain at least 10 queries: \(M(Q_8,3)\ge10\).

correctness.rationale: The signature map is injective exactly when the queries identify all vertices. Eight queries would force a bijection to all eight-bit strings and hence 128 positive answers per coordinate, contradicting ball size 93. Nine queries would have 256 distinct signatures with total weight 837, forcing precisely the weight-at-most-four nine-bit strings; that forces pairwise ball intersections of 29. Exact binomial counting gives intersection sizes 93, 58, 58, 38, 38, 20, 20, 0, 0 for center distances 0 through 8, so 29 is impossible. The included script verifies the finite arithmetic.

value.rationale: Nonadaptive ball search is a natural identification problem with sensor/query applications. The result strengthens the elementary information bound from eight to ten queries at the first dimension after the known seven-query Q7 example, using a reusable signature-weight obstruction rather than a routine computation. It gives a concrete boundary for future constructions without claiming the exact optimum.
